content.intro: Indexes and Ranges is lesson 62 in Strings, Characters, Arrays, and Ranges. Strings and arrays are indexed sequences, but text is encoded and may contain multiple code units per user-perceived character. Check boundaries and avoid unintended copies.
content.why_it_matters: Text and sequence bugs often come from assumptions about length, position, copying, or encoding. This lesson focuses on indexes and ranges and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

items.title: The index-from-end operator ^
items.text: Check bounds and copy behavior. Index-from-end and ranges make positions concise but do not remove boundary requirements.

items.title: The range operator ..
items.text: The `^` index counts backward from the end and the `..` range creates a slice boundary. The start is included and end is excluded; confirm length and allocation behavior before using a slice in a hot path.

items.title: Range-based slicing
